note: Where the Scout searches FIRST, by the language the profile speaks. DATA, not code: a portal that changes address, closes or opens is corrected here and nowhere else. `host` is a hint for the Scout, not a promise that it answers. access: search (a list the Scout reads), email (not searched: its alerts arrive by mail, so it counts as covered), closed (confirmed closed on a real run: 403, login wall, challenge; it counts as covered, say so). tier: core (covered BEFORE any minor source and required for `exhausted`) or minor. Retired (410, dead endpoint, taken off the lists): xing-jobs, bundesagentur-fuer-arbeit. broad_terms: an entry word on its own (internship); with level_terms they are the WIDE queries (query-kind broad): a portal that ANDs words answers 0 to a full title plus a place and hundreds to «praktik». api: a public, documented API address, no key, that answered 200 on the date in its hint (a hint, not a promise): the Scout asks it instead of the site's page. Only public pages and documented public APIs are read, and a page or address that the site's robots.txt disallows is not (access closed, with the reason in the hint). The kit of 03/11 for FR, DE, ES, PT, NL, BE, CH and AT was checked from the Mac with one request per address, nothing bypassed; a refusal seen only there closes nothing.
